entries.value: "Shared verbatim-JSON-per-id user store + CLI scaffold (#2158) for base-studio-code. bsc-blueprint and bsc-persona were byte-identical stores with a byte-identical `bsc <noun>` CLI; this is their single home, so each is a thin shim over one implementation. Backed by SQLite (#2983, one `<segment>.db` per store) with a one-time import of the legacy `<segment>/<id>.json` files; the public API + CLI are unchanged."

lead: # build.rs parses the committed graph store directly — see crates/graph-materialize/build.rs.

# crates reuse it without dragging the desktop app in. The hyphenated package name maps to the
# `bsc_json_store` crate name.

lead: # THE SHARED CRATE ROOT — this crate owns no source file at all. See
# crates/graph-materialize/crate_root.rs; the crate's own docs come from its record.
# Shared leaf utilities (#1646): the one cross-platform home-dir / `~/.base-studio-code` resolver, so
# every store CLI agrees on which dir it reads/writes.
# Shared CLI + SQLite helpers (#1621): `print_json` + `read_stdin_json` (the object-or-array stdin read
# the `set`-style command takes) AND, under `conn` (#2983), the connection plumbing this store now rides
# on — `open_db` (open + parent-dir create + busy_timeout) and `open_in_memory_db` (tests).
# Shared CLI scaffold (#1762): `CmdDoc`/`handle_help`/`unknown_command` help system + `resolve_store_path`.
# `preserve_order` — serde_json's Map becomes an insertion-ordered IndexMap instead of a BTreeMap.
# WHY IT IS HERE, AND WHY IT IS WORKSPACE-WIDE. This crate is the one whose job is reading and writing
# JSON records, so how a record SERIALIZES is its concern. But cargo unifies features per build, and 47
# crates in this workspace declare serde_json — so enabling it here enables it for all of them. That is
# the intended effect, stated out loud, because the alternative is it being switched on somewhere
# incidental and nobody knowing why key order suddenly matters.
# WHAT IT FIXES. Without it every re-serialization re-sorts keys alphabetically, so writing ONE field
# onto a seed record rewrites the whole file. Measured: placing `feature` on 294 packaged component
# seeds churned the key order in 280 of them, and the one line that actually changed was unreviewable
# inside the diff. `record_key_order_is_preserved` in this crate pins the behaviour.
# The SQLite backend (#2983): `bundled` compiles SQLite from source (matches plandb/skilldb/compliance)
# for cross-platform reliability. Same version as the sibling SQLite stores so the workspace shares one build.
